why: The tree predates the spelling the formatter now prefers: `Int` for `Int32`, `x?` for `x~`, and a trailing newline on most files. The code compiles and 1925 tests pass, so this is a distance to record, not a defect to fix here. Rewriting 621 files would also reflow the checked-in oracle goldens and break the byte identity the `golden` gate holds, so the reformat belongs in its own commit, if at all. The gate fails when this number moves in EITHER direction: a file becoming non-canonical is drift, and a file becoming canonical means this record is stale. Update it in the same commit as the change.
